title: Universal Music is launching an AI music platform with ElevenLabs
slides: Universal Music bets on AI — but why now?
ElevenLabs powers voice cloning for licensed tracks
Artists won't own the AI-generated versions
Your next release may compete with synthetic stars
Check if your catalog is already opted in
thread_text:
1. AI Copies Your Voice

Universal Music just inked a deal with ElevenLabs to clone voices from licensed tracks. If your song is in their catalog, your voice could become a synthetic star.

2. Why Universal Moves Now

Labels see AI as a new revenue stream, not a threat. They get upfront fees from tech partners while artists get zero ownership of the generated versions.

3. You Won't Own the Output

The deal explicitly excludes artists from owning AI-generated derivatives. Your vocal likeness can be licensed without your direct consent.

4. Synthetic Stars Are Coming

Your next release might compete with AI versions of yourself or other artists. The market will be flooded with legal, endless voice clones.

5. Check Your Opt-In Status

Go to your distributor's portal and search for AI training opt-out settings. If you do nothing, you're likely already opted in.
